Is my store listing affected by the move?
The listing stays the same. You upload the new version as an update to the same item, so reviews and installs remain attached to it. We prepare the package and notes for that.

Yes. Premium includes one extra browser package. Safari needs an Apple developer account and a Mac build step, so we confirm those details with you first.

desc:
Manifest V2 to V3 extension migration is the work Ecom Swift LLC does to move an older extension onto the current format, or port it to another browser, while keeping your users' saved settings intact.

## What is a Manifest V2 to V3 migration?

A Manifest V2 to V3 migration is the process of rewriting an extension so it follows the current rules that browsers enforce. The manifest file changes format. Background pages are replaced by service workers. Some request-handling and script-running methods are replaced by new ones. The goal is that the extension keeps doing the same job under the new rules.

Browsers have been phasing out the old format, and extensions that stay on it can be disabled or blocked from updates. Waiting does not remove the work, it only moves it to a worse moment.

## Why migrations need more care than a find-and-replace

A service worker is not a background page. It starts when needed and stops when idle, so any code that kept values in memory between events now loses them. Request blocking changes from running your own code on each request to declaring rules that the browser applies. Remote code is no longer allowed, so scripts must ship inside the package.

These differences touch the heart of how an extension works. A rushed move can break saved settings, stop alerts from arriving or change what a feature can do. A careful move tests each feature before and after, and says plainly where something now works differently.

## What a thorough migration includes

- A manifest rewritten for Manifest V3, with permissions split into required and optional.
- The background page rebuilt as a service worker that saves its state in storage.
- Request-blocking or modifying logic converted to declarative rules where it applies.
- Script injection updated to the current scripting methods.
- Alarms and events used in place of long-running timers.
- Saved user data carried across, with a migration script when formats change.
- Removal of remotely hosted code, bundled into the package instead.
- A feature-by-feature checklist, marked before and after the move.
- Tests in current Chrome and Edge, and in a second browser if you choose that package.
- Update notes you can share with your users.

## How we carry out the move

We start with an inventory: every feature, permission, stored value and outside call. Then we plan the order of the work, rebuild the manifest and worker, convert each feature and test it against the original behavior. Where a V2 trick has no V3 equivalent, we propose the closest alternative and show you the difference before we continue.

The Basic, Standard and Premium packages grow with the size of the extension. Basic moves a small extension and checks each feature. Standard handles a mid-size extension, request rules, stored settings and permission trimming. Premium covers a larger extension, a port to Firefox or a Safari package, a storage migration script and a period of fixes after release.

## Do and avoid during a migration

**Do:**
- List every feature and mark which ones are used most.
- Test with real saved data from an older install.
- Release to a small group before the full audience.
- Keep the old version available until the new one is proven.
- Tell users what changed and why.

**Avoid:**
- Treating the move as only a change to the manifest file.
- Keeping state in worker variables that disappear.
- Dropping a feature silently because it was hard to port.
- Requesting new permissions without a clear reason.
- Forgetting to update the store listing text that mentions old behavior.

## Who this is for

It suits an owner of an older extension that still has loyal users. It suits an agency that inherited a client tool built several years ago. And it suits a developer who wants a second browser supported without learning the differences first.

## What we need from you

Send the full source code and a description of the features you consider essential. If you have test accounts for the sites involved, mention them. Tell us which browsers you want to support after the move.

We never ask for passwords. We work from the code you share and, for publishing, we explain the steps or use the limited access your store dashboard allows. We reply after you order with an inventory sheet to confirm before work begins.
